title: Biggest merchant per city
statementMd:
For each city find the merchant with the highest total purchase spend (purchases are negative amounts; use absolute values). Show city, merchant, spend rounded to 2 decimals.

Expected columns: `city`, `merchant`, `spend`.

Tables: `customers`, `accounts`, `transactions`.

Row order does not matter.
hints: Join up to customers, group by city and merchant, rank within city.
solutionMd:
```sql
WITH s AS (SELECT c.city, t.merchant, SUM(-t.amount) AS spend FROM transactions t JOIN accounts a ON a.id = t.account_id JOIN customers c ON c.id = a.customer_id WHERE t.kind = 'purchase' GROUP BY c.city, t.merchant), r AS (SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY city ORDER BY spend DESC, merchant) AS rn FROM s) SELECT city, merchant, ROUND(spend, 2) AS spend FROM r WHERE rn = 1;
```

Compare with your own query; the result sets must match.
